Subject: Post-call recap — latency & topology (next steps)

Hi Amira / Ethan,

Thanks again for the deep-dive earlier — appreciate you walking through the Atlasful traffic patterns. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Pain points you confirmed
- p99 latency spikes on short prompts (search/autocomplete) during morning peak — currently 700–900ms
- Cost per 1M tokens is a blocker for broad rollout (current infra spend trend)
- KV cache miss amplification on multi-turn sessions; warmup costs for seq len ~512
- Compliance: audit logs and per-customer data partitioning are must-haves (SOC2 in 4 months)

Goals you shared
- Short prompt p99 target: <= 250ms (US region)
- Sustained throughput target: 350–500 qps for short inference (95 tokens average)
- Model fidelity: want to evaluate open models (Llama/Redwood-verified 70B variants) with 4-bit quantization acceptable if quality pass
- Minimum security: in-flight + at-rest encryption, KMS integration, audit log retention 1yr

Topology summary we discussed
- Prefer dedicated cluster model for predictable latency; fallback to hosted smaller variants for burst protection
- KV cache layer colocated on the inference nodes (local memcached-style) with a regional prefix cache to reduce cold fills
- Canary plan: start with 10% traffic on dedicated pool (non-critical routes), expand to 50% after 48h without regressions

Deliverables / next steps (owner + ETA)
- I attached a brief requirements sheet (atlasful-reqs.xlsx) and a topology sketch — please review and flag missing items (Owner: Laura, ETA: 2028-04-12)
- Redwood to produce a capacity + cost estimate for dedicated pool (Owner: Karthik, ETA: 2028-04-14)
- Security checklist & KMS integration notes (Owner: Markus, ETA: 2028-04-15)
- Schedule a 60-minute topology review with Atlasful infra + Redwood runtime engineers — propose times (Owner: Amira / Ethan)

Open clarifications we asked you about
- Typical multi-turn session length distribution (median, 80th) — you mentioned you would share the analytics export
- Any strict locality requirement (e.g., must stay in single AZ vs. multi-AZ)

If that all looks right, I can loop in Karthik and Markus this afternoon to start sizing. Happy to hop on a call Monday morning to walk the topology diagram live.

Best,

Amira / Ethan — quick update ahead of the Friday session: 

Answers to your clarifications
- KV cache TTL: recommended local TTL of 45–60s for the prefix cache combined with an LRU local in-memory layer. This reduces cold fills while keeping memory bounded. We'll include explicit cache hit-rate projections in the capacity sheet.
- Audit logs: we can provide request-level logs (request id, timestamp, model variant, tokens in/out, truncated user id) for dedicated deployments with a default 12-month retention. Token-level logs (raw token streams) are considered PII/PHI in some contexts and require a separate compliance agreement — we can discuss scope.
- Burst autoscaling: dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity and a fast-path routing policy; realistic warmup for large GPU-backed models is ~90–120s for heavy cold starts. For short prompts with KV cache warmed, we expect p99 to stay within target under 2x bursts; for 3x bursts we'll recommend leveraging hosted fallback model variant to absorb excess while dedicated scales.

Attached: topology-draft.png (sketch of dedicated + fallback routing) and redwood-tdr.pdf (technical deployment recommendations).
